Pricing: Editpad offers multiple plans: Weekly $5.99, Monthly $12.99, and Yearly $125. AI Productivity Tools For Sales Sales teams live in their inboxes, on calls, and inside their CRM. Every minute spent on admin is a minute not spent closing. When choosing AI productivity tools, a key factor is evaluating how much time or effort each tool saves compared to manual processes. The tools below tackle the four core sales bottlenecks: multi-channel prospecting, personalized copy, email management, and call intelligence. For a broader look at AI across the sales workflow, our guide to the best AI sales tools covers the full landscape. Apollo.io : Multi-Channel Prospecting and Outreach Category: Outbound prospecting and sequencing Apollo.io is an all-in-one B2B sales platform that combines a massive contact database (210M+ contacts) with built-in email sequencing, a dialer, and pipeline management. Instead of stitching together separate tools for data, outreach, and CRM, Apollo puts them all in one place. The AI features accelerate every stage of outbound. Advanced filters let you target prospects by technographics, funding rounds, hiring activity, and revenue. From there, you can build multi-step sequences with A/B testing, automate follow-ups, and track engagement, all without leaving the platform. The AI assistant helps with prospect research and call summaries. Best for: SDRs, AEs, and growth teams running structured outbound campaigns at scale. Pros: 210M+ contact database with advanced targeting filters Built-in email sequencing with A/B testing Dialer with call recording on higher-tier plans Integrates natively with Salesforce, HubSpot, and Outreach Cons: Credit-based system can drive unexpected costs at scale Phone number accuracy is inconsistent LinkedIn outreach still requires manual execution Advanced features are gated behind higher-tier plans Pricing: Free plan with limited credits. Basic at $49/user/month (annual). Professional at $79/user/month. Copy.ai : Sales Copy and GTM Workflows Category: Personalized outreach and sales enablement Copy.ai has evolved from a simple copywriting tool into a full go-to-market AI platform. Its standout capability for sales teams is the workflow builder, which chains together prospect research, personalized message generation, and CRM updates into automated sequences. Define your messaging framework, and Copy.ai handles personalization at scale. Where Apollo focuses on the data and delivery infrastructure, Copy.ai excels at the messaging layer. It generates the actual words: first-touch emails, follow-up sequences, LinkedIn connection messages, and objection-handling responses, all informed by CRM data and prospect context. Best for: Sales teams that need high-quality personalized messaging at scale, not just contact data. Pros: Workflow automations connect research, writing, and CRM updates Strong at generating variations for A/B testing CRM integrations for data-enriched personalization Generous free plan to test the waters Cons: Workflow builder has a learning curve Long-form content quality is inconsistent Most powerful features locked behind higher tiers Pricing: Free plan with 2,000 words per month. Pro plan starts at $49/month. If your sales team also needs help with pitch decks and proposals, our guide on creating AI-powered sales proposals walks through the workflow. We've also ranked the best AI tools for sales presentations specifically. Superhuman : Email Management Category: Email speed and prioritization For sales reps, email speed directly correlates with pipeline velocity. Superhuman is a premium email client built around that principle. Its AI drafts emails that match your personal writing style, summarizes long threads instantly, and surfaces the most important messages first through Split Inbox. The combination of keyboard shortcuts, AI drafting, and smart prioritization means reps spend less time managing email and more time on high-value conversations. Power users consistently report saving three to four hours per week. Read status tracking and snooze-based follow-up reminders ensure no deal-critical email slips through. Best for: Sales reps, AEs, and founders whose pipeline depends on fast, polished email communication. Pros: AI drafts genuinely match your personal writing tone Split Inbox auto-categorizes incoming mail by priority Keyboard-first design makes every action fast Read receipts and follow-up reminders built in Cons: $30/month is premium for an email client Limited to Gmail and Outlook Some power features have a learning curve Pricing: Starts at $30/month. Fireflies.ai : Call Intelligence Category: Meeting transcription and CRM sync Sales calls contain some of the most valuable data in any organization, but most of it disappears the moment the call ends. Fireflies.ai automatically joins your calls, transcribes them, extracts action items, and pushes everything into your CRM. The intelligence layer is what makes it particularly valuable for sales. It tracks sentiment throughout calls, flags buying signals, identifies objections, and builds a searchable archive of every prospect interaction. Over time, this makes deal reviews and coaching sessions far more productive. Best for: Sales teams that need call data flowing into their CRM and want intelligence from every prospect conversation. Pros: Deep CRM integrations (Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive) AI search across all call transcripts Sentiment analysis and topic tracking for deal intelligence Custom vocabulary training for industry jargon Cons: UI can feel cluttered with so many features Some integrations require higher-tier plans Audio quality heavily impacts transcription accuracy Pricing: Free plan with limited credits. Pro starts at $19/month per seat. Business plan and enterprise plans are also available, tailored for larger teams or organizations. Best AI Productivity Tools For Finance Finance teams deal with dense reports, time-sensitive data, and strict accuracy requirements. The AI tools best suited for finance help you process information faster, manage spend, and analyze documents without sacrificing the precision your work demands. Ramp : Expense Management and Spend Intelligence Category: Corporate spend management Ramp combines corporate cards with AI-driven expense management. It automatically categorizes transactions, flags duplicate charges, identifies subscription waste, and surfaces savings opportunities across your company's spend. AI receipt matching alone saves finance teams hours of manual reconciliation each month. What sets Ramp apart is its proactive intelligence. It doesn't just record what was spent; it identifies patterns. It flags vendors you're overpaying, unused subscriptions, and spending anomalies that might signal policy violations. For finance teams managing budgets across departments, this level of automated oversight is transformative. Best for: Finance teams at growing companies that need automated expense management with spend intelligence. Pros: AI transaction categorization and receipt matching Proactive savings recommendations and subscription monitoring Real-time spend visibility across departments Integrates with QuickBooks, NetSuite, Sage, and Xero Cons: Primarily designed for US-based companies Custom pricing requires a sales conversation Some advanced features take time to configure Pricing: Free corporate card program. Software pricing is custom. Perplexity AI : Research with Cited Sources Category: Financial research and due diligence Perplexity AI combines a search engine with an AI assistant to synthesize answers from multiple web sources with inline citations. For finance teams researching market trends, competitor benchmarks, regulatory changes, or data for financial models, it replaces the tedious cycle of opening tabs and manually piecing information together. Pro Search conducts multi-step research by asking clarifying questions and pulling from authoritative sources. For competitive analysis, market sizing, or due diligence research, it delivers citable answers in seconds rather than hours. Best for: Finance analysts who need fast, citable research for reports and strategic decisions. Pros: Inline citations on every answer for source verification Pro Search handles complex multi-step queries Clean interface built for research, not content generation Collections for organizing ongoing research threads Cons: Free plan limits Pro Search queries Occasionally surfaces outdated sources Not a replacement for specialized databases like Bloomberg or PitchBook Pricing: Free plan with basic search. Pro at $20/month. NotebookLM : Source-Grounded Document Analysis Category: Document analysis and synthesis Google's NotebookLM takes a fundamentally different approach to AI research. You upload your own sources (PDFs, docs, websites, YouTube videos) and the AI works exclusively with that material. Every insight is grounded in what you provided, with zero risk of hallucinated information from external sources. This source-grounding is critical for finance, where accuracy isn't optional. Upload earnings reports, 10-K filings, board presentations, or financial models and ask questions like "What were the key risk factors across these three filings?" The AI stays strictly within your material. The Audio Overview feature also generates podcast-style discussions of your uploads, which is a surprisingly effective way to absorb dense documents. Best for: Finance professionals analyzing stacks of dense documents who need accuracy and source traceability. Pros: Completely source-grounded, no hallucinated external data Supports PDFs, Google Docs, web pages, YouTube, and more Audio Overview turns dense documents into listenable content Free to use Cons: Only works with content you upload, no web search Limited to 50 sources per notebook Audio quality varies with source complexity Pricing: Free. Best AI Productivity Tools For Business Ops Operations teams are the connective tissue of any organization. They manage the systems, processes, and workflows that keep everything running. These tools help ops teams automate repetitive work, optimize schedules, and maintain a single source of truth for company knowledge. Increasingly, some business ops tools now include an 'ai studio' - an integrated feature for automating workflows and facilitating data-driven decision-making. For founders and ops leaders building their full tool stack, our guide to the best AI tools for founders covers how these pieces fit together. Notion AI : Workspace and Knowledge Management Category: Docs, wikis, and project management Notion has become the default workspace for startups and scaling teams, and its AI layer makes it significantly more powerful. Notion AI summarizes pages, generates content, extracts action items, auto-fills database properties, and answers questions across your entire workspace. The Q&A feature is the standout for ops teams. Instead of searching through dozens of wiki pages or digging through Slack, ask Notion AI a question and it pulls the answer from your knowledge base. For teams managing SOPs, vendor docs, onboarding guides, and project trackers all in one place, this alone is worth the AI add-on cost. Best for: Teams already using Notion who want AI layered into their existing workflows. Pros: AI works contextually within your existing workspace Q&A searches across all pages, databases, and wikis Flexible enough for docs, project boards, CRM, and more Massive template gallery Cons: AI add-on cost scales with team size Can be overwhelming to set up from scratch AI features are most valuable within Notion's own ecosystem Pricing: Free personal plan. Plus at $12/month. AI add-on is $10/member/month. For startups building their ops stack, our guide to the best AI tools for startups shows how Notion fits into a broader system. Zapier : Workflow Automation Category: Cross-platform automation Zapier connects over 6,000 apps and lets you build automated workflows without writing code. When a lead fills a form, Zapier can add them to your CRM, notify sales in Slack, and trigger a welcome email. When an invoice is paid in Stripe, it updates your spreadsheet, sends a confirmation, and logs the transaction. Its AI features now let you describe automations in plain language and Zapier builds them for you. The newer Agents feature creates AI assistants that can take multi-step actions across your tool stack. For ops teams managing dozens of cross-platform processes, Zapier eliminates hours of manual data transfer and reduces copy-paste errors. Best for: Operations teams automating cross-platform workflows without developer support. Pros: Connects to virtually every SaaS tool in your stack Natural language automation builder Agents feature for multi-step AI-powered actions Extensive template library and battle-tested reliability Cons: Multi-step Zaps require paid plans Debugging failed automations can be frustrating Per-task pricing gets expensive at high volumes Pricing: Free plan with unlimited single-step Zaps. Paid plans start at $29.99/month. Motion : Task and Calendar Management Category: Auto-scheduling and prioritization Motion takes your tasks, deadlines, and meetings and automatically schedules everything into your calendar. As priorities shift or meetings get added, it re-optimizes your day continuously. It eliminates the daily ritual of staring at a to-do list and deciding what to work on next. For ops leaders juggling strategic projects alongside a packed meeting schedule, Motion ensures important work actually gets calendar time instead of languishing on a list. Team features surface capacity issues before anyone misses a deadline. Best for: Ops managers and team leads who want their calendar to reflect actual priorities. Pros: Auto-scheduling removes daily planning friction Continuous re-optimization as priorities change Team capacity planning prevents overload Combines tasks, calendar, and project views Cons: $34/month is steep compared to simpler task managers Requires willingness to let AI manage your schedule Mobile app less polished than desktop Pricing: Plans start at $34/month. Clockwise : Calendar Optimization Category: Focus time protection and team scheduling Clockwise focuses on one specific problem and solves it well: protecting focus time. It analyzes your team's calendars and automatically moves flexible meetings to create longer uninterrupted blocks for deep work. Its AI assistant, Prism, handles availability queries, scheduling, and conflict resolution through a chat interface. The real value appears at the team level. Clockwise doesn't just optimize your schedule; it optimizes everyone's, finding meeting slots that preserve focus time for the entire group. For cross-functional ops teams trying to protect maker time, it's one of the most impactful tools you can adopt. Best for: Teams struggling with calendar fragmentation who want to protect deep work time. Pros: Automatically moves flexible meetings to protect focus blocks Team-wide optimization, not just individual Easy availability sharing for external scheduling Works with Google Calendar and Outlook Cons: Greatest value requires team-wide adoption Limited benefit for solo professionals Free plan is heavily restricted Pricing: Free plan with basics. Paid plans start at $6.75/month, billed annually. Best AI Productivity Tools For HR HR teams handle some of the most communication-intensive work in any organization: hiring, onboarding, training, performance management, and employee engagement. The tools below address three distinct HR workflows that AI can meaningfully accelerate. Synthesia : Training and Onboarding Videos Category: Scalable video content for L&D Producing training and onboarding videos traditionally requires cameras, studios, and presenters that most HR teams don't have budget for. Synthesia lets you generate professional-looking videos from a text script using AI avatars. Write the script, choose an avatar, and the tool produces a polished video in minutes. The real value for HR is the update cycle. When a policy changes, you edit the script and regenerate rather than re-filming. With 230+ avatar options, 140+ languages, and custom avatar creation, Synthesia scales video production in ways traditional filming simply cannot. Best for: HR and L&D teams that need scalable training, onboarding, and internal communication videos. Pros: No filming equipment, studio, or on-camera talent required 140+ languages with natural-sounding voiceovers Scripts can be updated and regenerated instantly Custom avatars for brand consistency Cons: AI avatars still look noticeably artificial in some contexts Limited control over gestures and expressions May feel impersonal for sensitive communications Pricing: Free plan with limited minutes. Starter at $29/month. Textio : Inclusive Hiring Language Category: Job descriptions and recruitment messaging The language in your job descriptions directly impacts who applies. Textio uses AI to analyze and optimize hiring content for inclusivity, clarity, and effectiveness. It flags phrases that statistically discourage candidates from underrepresented groups, suggests alternatives, and scores your job listings based on how likely they are to attract diverse, qualified applicants. Beyond job descriptions, Textio also helps with recruiter outreach messages, interview feedback, and performance review language. For HR teams focused on improving hiring outcomes and reducing bias in their written communications, it provides a data-driven approach that generic writing tools simply can't match. Best for: HR and talent acquisition teams committed to inclusive, effective hiring language. Pros: Data-driven analysis of language bias in job postings Scores listings on predicted inclusivity and effectiveness Covers recruiter outreach, feedback, and reviews beyond just job descriptions Benchmarks your language against industry data Cons: Custom pricing requires a sales conversation Most valuable at scale with high-volume hiring Focused scope means it won't replace general writing tools Pricing: Custom pricing based on company size and usage. Leapsome : Performance Management and Engagement Category: Reviews, goals, and employee development Performance reviews are one of the most dreaded processes in any organization, for managers and employees alike. Leapsome uses AI to streamline the entire cycle: writing review drafts, calibrating feedback, tracking goals, running engagement surveys, and identifying development gaps. It connects performance data with engagement insights so HR teams can spot trends before they become turnover problems. The AI writing assistant helps managers craft constructive, specific feedback faster. Instead of staring at a blank review form, managers get AI-generated draft summaries based on goal progress and peer feedback, which they then refine. For HR leaders, the platform surfaces team-level patterns in engagement and performance that would take weeks to compile manually. Best for: HR teams at mid-size and enterprise companies looking to modernize their performance and engagement processes. Pros: AI-assisted review writing saves managers hours per cycle Connects performance data with engagement survey insights Goal tracking, 1:1 management, and learning paths in one platform Strong analytics for identifying team-level trends Cons: Custom pricing means no self-serve sign-up Requires organizational buy-in for full value Setup and configuration take time for larger orgs Pricing: Custom pricing based on company size and modules selected. Mindgrasp: AI-Powered Study Assistant for Smarter Learning Category: Education, Study & Research Mindgrasp AI is a powerful AI study Tool designed to help professionals learn faster by turning complex materials into clear, digestible insights. Instead of spending hours reading through dense textbooks, PDFs, or watching long lectures, users can upload their content and instantly generate summaries, notes, and key takeaways. The platform supports multiple formats, including PDFs, videos, online articles, and lecture recordings, making it a flexible companion for modern learning. Its AI can break down difficult concepts, highlight important points, and even answer questions based on the uploaded material, helping users move from passive reading to active understanding. One standout feature is its ability to convert content into structured notes and study guides, allowing users to review information more efficiently before exams or presentations. By automating the most time-consuming parts of studying, Mindgrasp helps learners focus on comprehension rather than information overload. Best for: Professionals, researchers, and lifelong learners who want to quickly understand and retain information from large or complex study materials. Pros: Quickly summarizes long documents, videos, and lectures Supports multiple content formats for flexible learning Helps generate structured notes and study guides Saves significant time during research and revision Cons: Requires uploading materials (no broad web search capability) Accuracy depends on the quality of the input content Advanced features may require a paid plan Pricing: Free plan available; premium plans unlock additional features and higher usage limits. RemNote: AI-Powered Note-Taking and Flashcard Creation Category: Education, Learning & Knowledge Retention RemNote is an advanced note-taking and learning platform built for students, researchers, and professionals who want to retain information more effectively. What makes the platform stand out is its integrated AI flashcard generator , which can instantly turn notes, PDFs, and study materials into interactive flashcards for active recall and spaced repetition learning. The platform combines document organization, linked knowledge management, and AI-powered study tools into a single workspace. Users can create structured notes while automatically generating flashcards from key concepts, definitions, and highlighted text, reducing the manual effort typically required for exam preparation or long-term learning. RemNote also supports spaced repetition scheduling, helping learners review information at the optimal time to improve memory retention. Its flexible knowledge graph and bi-directional linking system make it especially useful for managing complex subjects, research projects, or professional certifications. Best for: Students, lifelong learners, researchers, and professionals who want to streamline studying, improve retention, and automate flashcard creation from their learning materials. Pros: Built-in AI flashcard generator for faster study workflows Combines note-taking, knowledge management, and spaced repetition Supports active recall learning techniques for better retention Ideal for organizing large volumes of interconnected information Cons: Might only be useful for teams which require frequent knowledge upskilling Pricing: Has a free trial with paid plans starting at $4 per month. Best AI Productivity Tools For Design Venngage: AI-Generated Designs for Marketing, HR, and Sales Category: AI design and visual content Venngage is an AI design tool that helps you create social media posts, infographics, presentations, reports, posters, proposals, carousels, and more. If you're in marketing, you're creating campaign visuals and social media graphics. If you're in HR, you're building onboarding guides, training materials, and internal documents. If you're in sales, you're working on pitch decks, proposals, and client presentations. All of it takes time, and most teams don't have a designer available for every request. Venngage's AI Design Generator cuts that time down to minutes. Describe what you need in a text prompt, and it generates a ready-to-use design. Once your design is ready, you can use AI Designer to edit it by simply typing the changes you want. You can also swap color palettes to see different looks, generate icons and images directly inside the editor, and adjust layouts without touching a single design element manually. Plus, with the Brand Kit, it's easy to add your logo, fonts, and brand colors in one click instead of searching for assets or entering hex codes every time. Best for: Marketing, HR, and sales teams that regularly produce visual content across multiple formats and need consistent, on-brand output without relying on a designer for every request. Pros: Text prompt to finished design in minutes, including social media graphics, infographics, carousels, posters, proposals, presentations, and more 10,000+ templates across business categories AI writing assistant that drafts, rewrites, and refines text directly inside your design AI image generator for creating custom visuals without leaving the editor Automated charts and graphs from CSV or spreadsheet uploads Reusable templates for repeat content Live shareable links for team collaboration Cons: No video or animated content, static designs only Collaboration features are on paid plans Pricing: Free plan available. Premium from $19/month. Business from $49/month per user. Enterprise from $499/month. Frequently Asked Questions What is the best AI tool for productivity in 2026? There's no single "best" tool because the answer depends entirely on where you spend most of your time. For marketing teams building presentations, Alai delivers designer-quality output with the least manual effort. For sales teams managing high-volume email, Superhuman consistently saves users three to four hours per week. For operations teams connecting their app stack, Zapier automates cross-platform workflows without code. The best approach is to identify your team's biggest time sink and pick the tool that directly addresses it. Are AI productivity tools worth the cost? For most knowledge workers, yes. The ROI calculation is straightforward: if a tool costs $20-50/month and saves you even five hours of work per month, you're getting your time back at a fraction of your hourly rate. The real risk isn't overspending on a useful tool; it's spending money on tools you never fully adopt. Start with free plans or trials, build the habit, and only upgrade when you're confident the tool is delivering measurable value. Can AI tools replace human workers? No. AI productivity tools are designed to handle the repetitive, time-consuming parts of work: drafting first versions, categorizing data, scheduling meetings, transcribing calls, and generating design layouts. They compress the time between "blank page" and "solid first draft." But the strategic thinking, creative judgment, relationship-building, and nuanced decision-making that drive business outcomes still require humans. The most productive teams use AI to clear the busywork so they can spend more time on the high-value work that only people can do. How do I get my team to actually use AI tools? Adoption is the biggest challenge with any new tool. A few things that consistently work: start with one tool that addresses a pain point your team already complains about (not something you think they should care about). Have one person become the internal champion who builds the initial workflows and shows others. Set a specific two-week trial period where the team commits to using the tool daily. And make it easy by choosing tools that integrate with software your team already uses rather than requiring them to switch platforms entirely. What's the difference between AI productivity tools and ChatGPT? ChatGPT (and similar general-purpose chatbots like Claude and Gemini) can do a bit of everything: answer questions, write drafts, summarize documents, brainstorm ideas. But that breadth comes with trade-offs. Dedicated AI tools are purpose-built for specific workflows and typically produce significantly better results within their domain. An AI presentation maker like Alai will generate better slides than ChatGPT. An AI email client will manage your inbox better than pasting emails into a chatbot. Think of ChatGPT as a versatile generalist and dedicated tools as specialists: you want both, used for the right tasks. Are free AI productivity tools any good? Several excellent tools offer genuinely useful free plans. Alai gives you 200 AI credits with all premium design elements. Buffer's free plan includes three social channels with unlimited AI assistant access. NotebookLM is completely free with powerful source-grounded research. Grammarly's free tier covers core grammar checking. The free plans are typically enough to test whether a tool fits your workflow before committing to a paid plan. The main limitations on free tiers are usually volume caps (credits, channels, or features) rather than quality differences. How do I measure the ROI of AI productivity tools? Track two things: time saved and output quality. For time, measure how long a recurring task takes before and after adopting the tool. If building a weekly campaign report took three hours and now takes 30 minutes, that's quantifiable. For quality, look at downstream metrics: are your presentations winning more pitches? Are your sales emails getting higher response rates? Are fewer errors slipping through your documents? Most teams find the time savings alone justify the investment, but quality improvements often deliver even larger returns. Can AI productivity tools work together? Absolutely, and this is where the biggest productivity gains come from. For example, Fireflies.ai can transcribe a sales call and extract action items, Copy.ai can draft the follow-up email based on those notes, and Zapier can log the entire interaction in your CRM automatically. Alai's API lets you generate presentations programmatically from CRM data or analytics dashboards. The key is choosing tools with strong integrations (APIs, Zapier connections, or native integrations) so data flows between them without manual copy-pasting. What AI tools are best for small teams or solopreneurs? Small teams should prioritize tools with generous free tiers and low per-user costs. Alai (free plan with 200 credits), Buffer (free for 3 channels), Notion AI ($10/month add-on), and Perplexity AI (free for basic research) are all strong starting points. Avoid tools with per-seat pricing that scales quickly. For solopreneurs specifically, the highest-impact combination is usually an AI writing/email tool plus a presentation tool plus a workflow automation tool. That covers the three biggest time sinks for most solo operators. How often should I re-evaluate my AI tool stack? At minimum, once per quarter. The AI landscape is evolving faster than almost any other software category. Tools ship major updates monthly, pricing structures change, and new entrants appear regularly. Set a calendar reminder to audit your tools every 90 days. Ask: is this tool still saving me time? Has something better launched? Am I actually using all the features I'm paying for? This prevents both overspending on underused tools and missing out on better alternatives. Final Thoughts: Building an AI-Powered Workflow Picking the right tools is only half the equation. The teams that get the most out of AI are the ones that treat adoption as a habit-building exercise, not a one-time purchase decision. Start by embedding one tool deeply into a single workflow. Let your marketing team spend two weeks using Alai for every deck before adding Jasper for content. Let your sales reps live in Superhuman for a month before layering in Apollo for outbound. Depth beats breadth every time when it comes to AI adoption. Once a tool is producing consistent results, look for compounding opportunities. The real productivity leap happens when tools work together: Fireflies transcribes the sales call, Copy.ai drafts the follow-up, and Zapier logs the whole interaction in your CRM without anyone touching a keyboard. These connected workflows are where AI moves from a convenience to a competitive advantage. Most AI tools are designed to integrate with existing workflows and can be layered for even greater productivity gains. The landscape will keep evolving. New tools will launch, existing ones will add features, and pricing will shift. But if you’ve built the organizational muscle of reaching for AI when repetitive work shows up, you’ll be in a position to absorb those changes rather than scramble to keep up. The best time to start was six months ago. The second best time is today. Want to go deeper on specific use cases? Explore our guides on AI tools for startups , AI-powered sales proposals , AI presentation makers for consultants , and how to make AI slides that actually look designer-made . Author's note: I update this list every 2-3 months based off new tools I have tested. Last updated as of 5th June, 2026.

title: TIC Solutions Completes Three Strategic Acquisitions, Expanding Its Technical Capabilities and Geographic Reach
summary: - Expands TIC Solutions’ capabilities and geographic reach across key end markets - - Acquired businesses contribute a total of approximately $90 million of annualized revenue - - Accretive to TIC Solutions’ “3/18/85” long-term financial targets - TIC Solutions, Inc. (NYSE: TIC) (the “ Company ”, “ TIC ” or “ TIC Solutions ”), a leading provider of tech-enabled asset integrity, engineering, and geospatial services, announced today that it has recently completed the acquisitions of we-do-IT, Inc. (“WDI”), GeoVerra Holdings Inc. (“GeoVerra”), and Core Group Limited (“Core Group”) (collectively, the “Acquisitions”). The Acquisitions expand TIC Solutions’ technical capabilities and strengthen its presence across key markets and geographies, including Canada and Europe. The acquired businesses bring complementary technical expertise, long-standing customer relationships and experienced teams that are expected to support cross-selling and growth across TIC Solutions’ integrated platform.
body_text: View All News TIC Solutions Completes Three Strategic Acquisitions, Expanding Its Technical Capabilities and Geographic Reach August 18, 2026 Download (opens in new window) - Expands TIC Solutions’ capabilities and geographic reach across key end markets - - Acquired businesses contribute a total of approximately $90 million of annualized revenue - - Accretive to TIC Solutions’ “3/18/85” long-term financial targets - HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- TIC Solutions, Inc. (NYSE: TIC) (the “ Company ”, “ TIC ” or “ TIC Solutions ”), a leading provider of tech-enabled asset integrity, engineering, and geospatial services, announced today that it has recently completed the acquisitions of we-do-IT, Inc. (“WDI”), GeoVerra Holdings Inc. (“GeoVerra”), and Core Group Limited (“Core Group”) (collectively, the “Acquisitions”). The Acquisitions expand TIC Solutions’ technical capabilities and strengthen its presence across key markets and geographies, including Canada and Europe. The acquired businesses bring complementary technical expertise, long-standing customer relationships and experienced teams that are expected to support cross-selling and growth across TIC Solutions’ integrated platform. Together, the acquired businesses generate approximately $90 million of annualized revenue. “We are excited to welcome the WDI, GeoVerra, and Core Group teams to the TIC family. Each business has an excellent reputation in its respective market, experienced leadership and complementary expertise that strengthens our existing platform,” said Ben Heraud, Chief Executive Officer of TIC Solutions. “Together, they create new opportunities to cross-sell our capabilities and better serve clients across the asset lifecycle. We look forward to supporting their continued growth as part of the TIC family.” Colorado-based WDI provides specialized data management and software integration services for utility companies across North America. This acquisition enhances TIC’s ability to help utility clients modernize their power grids and manage complex digital infrastructure through long-term and recurring service agreements. Headquartered in Edmonton, Alberta, GeoVerra is one of Canada’s leading surveying and geomatics companies, specializing in mapping, land services, and high-tech data capture. GeoVerra supports clients across the infrastructure, energy, utilities, transportation, and natural resource sectors. This acquisition establishes a meaningful geospatial and engineering footprint in Canada for TIC by integrating the existing capabilities of Acuren and NV5 to support the asset lifecycle. UK-based Core Group provides commissioning and commissioning management services across complex building systems. This acquisition adds mission-critical commissioning expertise across data centers, commercial buildings, healthcare, education, transportation and other infrastructure end markets, while establishing a platform for further growth in Europe. The Acquisitions are expected to be accretive to TIC Solutions’ “3/18/85” long-term financial targets, excluding transaction and integration-related costs. The purchase price for each Acquisition was funded with cash on hand. About TIC Solutions TIC Solutions is a leading provider of tech-enabled asset integrity, engineering, and geospatial services. The Company delivers mission-critical services across the full lifecycle of industrial assets, buildings, and public infrastructure, from planning and construction through operations and ongoing maintenance. Operating across North America and select international markets, TIC Solutions serves a diversified client base across its principal end markets: oil and gas, industrials, buildings, power and utilities, infrastructure, natural resources, and aerospace and defense, including federal, state, and municipal customers across public-sector applications, with exposure to data centers and other high-growth industries. TIC Solutions operates through three reportable segments: Inspection & Mitigation; Consulting & Engineering; and Geospatial, providing asset integrity services, engineering and advisory solutions, and data-driven asset intelligence capabilities. The Company’s services are frequently non-discretionary, compliance-driven and typically recurring in nature, delivered by more than 12,000 professionals across over 250 locations. For more information, please visit www.ticsolutions.com . title: Biosimilars for Simponi: A Guide for UC Patients
summary: Understand Immgolis coverage and prepare for a switch from Simponi.
body_text: For people with ulcerative colitis, the first Simponi biosimilar arrived in the United States in May 2026. Its approval adds a new subcutaneous golimumab option, while the closely related product names make careful checking important. Immgolis references Simponi and includes ulcerative colitis. Immgolis Intri references Simponi Aria and has a different set of approved uses. Knowing which product your prescription names is the starting point for any coverage or switching conversation. The first Simponi biosimilar for ulcerative colitis The FDA approved Immgolis and Immgolis Intri in May 2026 as the first biosimilars to Simponi and Simponi Aria. Accord BioPharma is the FDA applicant for both. Immgolis is a subcutaneous injection and is the product relevant to adult ulcerative colitis. Immgolis Intri is an intravenous infusion whose approved uses are rheumatology indications. For adult ulcerative colitis, the Immgolis prescribing information specifies 200 mg under the skin at week zero, 100 mg at week two, and 100 mg at week six and every four weeks afterward. A new prescription should preserve the clinician's intended dose and timing. Confirm the full product name, strength, pen or syringe presentation, and training needs before the first delivery. What interchangeable means for Immgolis FDA designated both products as interchangeable with their respective reference drugs. Under U.S. law, an interchangeable biosimilar may be substituted for its reference product at the pharmacy without prescriber intervention, subject to state pharmacy law. FDA also emphasizes that interchangeability addresses substitution and gives no product a safety or effectiveness ranking. All approved biosimilars must meet the agency's standard of high similarity with no clinically meaningful difference in safety, purity, or potency. The agency's interchangeability explainer provides that distinction. Patients can still ask to be told which product is dispensed. Record the brand and nonproprietary name from the carton, including its suffix, and check that it matches the medication list. If a clinician intends a specific product, that direction should be reflected in the prescription and handled according to state law. Questions about substitution can be addressed by the gastroenterology office and dispensing pharmacy before a shipment is released. Insurance and availability implications FDA approval creates a pathway for use, while real-world access depends on plan formularies, contracting, pharmacy inventory, and launch timing. Self-injected golimumab is commonly handled through a specialty pharmacy, while patients should verify which benefit and dispensing channel their plan uses. Ask whether Immgolis is preferred, whether Simponi remains covered, and whether a new prior authorization is required. Also confirm the allowed specialty pharmacy, effective date, quantity limit, and exact out-of-pocket amount. The FDA patient guide explains that insurance reimbursement sits outside FDA's role and directs patients to their insurer for coverage details. The Crohn's & Colitis Foundation recommends asking about cost, assistance programs, the timing of a required change, and appeal rights. Because this product was approved recently, checking current stocking and plan status is more reliable than assuming that approval means immediate access. Preparing for a switch from Simponi Before changing products, save the authorization, last Simponi dose date, delivery schedule, and a baseline of bowel frequency, bleeding, urgency, pain, and recent biomarkers. After the first Immgolis doses, log injection dates, device problems, injection-site reactions, and changes in ulcerative colitis symptoms. These records give the care team a clearer timeline if the shipment is delayed or symptoms change. When the first shipment arrives, compare the carton with the prescription and confirm the brand, suffix, strength, quantity, expiration date, and storage instructions. Ask a pharmacist or manufacturer support program for device training if the injection steps differ from the previous pen or syringe. Schedule the refill early enough to resolve a rejected claim before the next four-week dose. Save the pharmacy's shipment confirmation and the insurer's call reference number with the dosing log. If the insurer announces a future formulary change before the pharmacy can fill Immgolis, ask for a temporary continuity authorization. Give the plan the next dose date and current pharmacy's inventory response, then send the case number to the gastroenterology office. Written timing details help the plan address an access gap before it becomes a missed dose. Golimumab products carry important safety warnings. The Immgolis label has a boxed warning for serious infections and malignancy and directs clinicians to test for tuberculosis before treatment. Contact the treating team promptly about signs of infection, a suspected severe reaction, a missed dose, or worsening ulcerative colitis. The switch should keep the prescribed schedule intact while the insurer, specialty pharmacy, and gastroenterology office align on the exact product. This article is for educational purposes and is not medical advice. It is researched against current AGA clinical guidelines and peer-reviewed sources. Always discuss treatment decisions with your care team. Biosimilars for Tysabri: A Guide for Crohn's Disease ›

title: Toyota TRD 3000GT Is a Rare, Race-Inspired Supra, and It Could Be Yours
summary: The Mk IV Toyota Supra has become one of the most valuable and sought-after Japanese sports cars of its era, but some variants of it are rarer than others. Broad Arrow will auction off what many consider one of the most desirable Mk IVs during its The Quail Auction 2026: It’s one of 35 Toyota […]
body_text: The Mk IV Toyota Supra has become one of the most valuable and sought-after Japanese sports cars of its era, but some variants of it are rarer than others. Broad Arrow will auction off what many consider one of the most desirable Mk IVs during its The Quail Auction 2026: It’s one of 35 Toyota TRD 3000GT examples built, and it’s the only one based on an American-market car. Production of the Mk IV (A80-gen) Supra started in 1993, and aftermarket tuners weren’t the only ones eager to modify it. Toyota used the platform to create a race car for the inaugural Japanese Grand Touring Championship to help cement the model’s performance credentials. Meanwhile, Toyota Racing Development (TRD) drew inspiration from the track-bound Supra to develop a more powerful street-legal evolution of the A80. Known as the TRD 3000GT, it made its global debut at the 1994 edition of the Tokyo Auto Salon. The modifications made included wider wheels tucked under punched-out wheel arches, a larger intercooler hidden behind a redesigned front bumper, a model-specific hood with four cooling vents, and a body kit. Broad Arrow explains that these parts were available individually through TRD, so anyone could buy a hood or a rear spoiler and put it on their Supra. Only 35 units were fully converted in-house by Toyota and fitted with a TRD 3000GT identification plate, however. This is one of those cars. Broad Arrow Auctions Broad Arrow Auctions Broad Arrow Auctions Broad Arrow Auctions Broad Arrow Auctions Assigned chassis number JT2JA82J5R0011586, the example in Broad Arrow’s catalog started life as a 1994 Supra RZ fitted with the six-speed manual transmission. It was delivered new in California, where it was purchased by a Japanese tourist visiting the United States. The first owner shipped it back to Japan in early 1994 and had it converted to full TRD 3000GT spec in May 2001. The car stayed in the Tokyo area until it was sold to a Danish collector in 2007. The current owner purchased it in 2015, and it has covered about 1500 miles over the last 11 years. Its odometer consequently shows about 68,000 miles, which is fairly low for a 32-year-old car. It hasn’t been kept fully stock, however. Broad Arrow reports several period-correct modifications such as an HKS Vein Pressure Converter and Graphic Control Computer ECU, Recaro seats, carbon fiber interior trim, and Defi gauges. With the modifications, the twin-turbocharged, 3.0-liter straight-six makes nearly 500 horsepower according to a dyno test done in Denmark in 2009. That’s a big jump over the stock Supra’s 320-horse rating, but it’s not entirely surprising considering the massive amount of power that the famed 2JZ-GTE engine is capable of handling. This TRD 3000GT retains its six-speed manual gearbox. Broad Arrow notes that this Toyota TRD 3000GT is offered on international documents, and that getting a U.S. title will require additional processing time. For peace of mind, the sale includes a Carfax report that lists a single entry in 1993 and a clean CarVX report (think of it as the Japanese equivalent to Carfax) that lists no accidents, mileage inconsistencies, or other potential problems. This rare piece of Toyota history is estimated to sell for between $500,000 and $800,000 when it crosses the block on August 13 . title: AWS IAM identity federation to external services is now available in AWS European Sovereign Cloud Region
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with AWS IAM identity federation to external services is now available in AWS European Sovereign Cloud Region
body_text: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) now enables AWS workloads in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region to securely authenticate with external services using short-lived JSON Web Tokens (JWTs). The AWS European Sovereign Cloud is an independent cloud for Europe entirely located within the European Union (EU), designed to help customers meet their evolving sovereignty requirements. With outbound identity federation, AWS workloads can securely authenticate with third-party cloud providers, SaaS providers, and self-hosted applications without using long-term credentials or implementing complex workarounds. Customers can exchange their AWS IAM credentials for cryptographically signed, short-lived JWTs, providing a simple and secure mechanism to access external services. These tokens contain rich context about the AWS workloads, enabling external services to implement fine-grained access control. Administrators can control access to token generation and enforce token properties (such as lifetime, audience, and signing algorithms) using IAM policies and audit token usage using CloudTrail logs, allowing them to meet their organization's security and compliance requirements. To learn more, visit the outbound identity federation product page , see the IAM user guide , or read the AWS News Blog Post .

title: ProQR Announces Second Quarter 2026 Operating and Financial Results
summary: ProQR is a clinical stage biotech company based in the Netherlands that discovers and develops unique RNA-based therapies for severe genetic disorders.
body_text: First clinical validation of Axiomer™ RNA editing established through NTCP modulation with positive AX-0810 clinical target engagement data; full Phase 1 dataset to be presented at a medical or scientific conference later this year Multiple clinical milestones, including initial AX-0811 Phase 1 data expected by year-end 2026, followed in H1 2027 by: biliary atresia IIT initiation and initial data, initial AX-0422 (IDUA) patient data in MPS I Hurler syndrome, and advancement of AX-2911 (PNPLA3) to the clinic Strengthened balance sheet through $59.2 million financing during the quarter; ended Q2 2026 with € 117.1 million cash and cash equivalents, supporting runway through mid-2028 LEIDEN, Netherlands & CAMBRIDGE, Mass., Aug. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- ProQR Therapeutics N.V. (Nasdaq: PRQR) (ProQR), a clinical-stage company dedicated to changing lives through transformative RNA therapies based on its proprietary Axiomer™ RNA editing technology platform, today reported its financial and operating results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, and provided a business update. “The second quarter marked an important inflection point for ProQR as we established the first clinical validation of our Axiomer RNA editing platform by modulating NTCP with AX-0810,” said Daniel A. de Boer, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of ProQR. “We believe these data, together with the significant unmet need that remains in cholestatic liver diseases, including biliary atresia, support the continued advancement of our NTCP franchise. Combined with our recent financing, we are well positioned to deliver a series of important clinical milestones, including presentation of the full AX-0810 Phase 1 dataset later this year, initial Phase 1 data from AX-0811 by year end, initiation of our biliary atresia clinical program and initial data in the first half of 2027, and continued advancement of our MPS I Hurler syndrome and MASH programs. Together, these milestones reflect ProQR’s evolution into a multi-program clinical-stage RNA editing company, strengthen the growing body of evidence supporting the broader potential of our Axiomer platform, and bring us closer to delivering transformative RNA editing therapies for patients.” Recent Progress and Anticipated Upcoming Events First Clinical Validation of Axiomer and Next Milestones with NTCP Franchise ProQR’s NTCP RNA editing approach is designed to modulate NTCP and reduce bile acid uptake directly in hepatocytes, with the goal of reducing intrahepatic cholestasis. In June, ProQR announced positive AX-0810 Phase 1 target engagement data from healthy volunteers, establishing the first clinical validation of the Company’s proprietary Axiomer RNA editing platform. Key findings included: Up to 8-fold increase in total serum bile acids (6 mg/kg) exceeding the Company’s pre-defined 2-fold threshold for meaningful NTCP modulation; Dose-dependent changes in conjugated bile acids, together with concordant changes in total serum bile acids and TUDCA, supporting the therapeutic rationale that modulating NTCP reduces the accumulation of toxic bile acids in the liver; Favorable safety and tolerability profile observed with AX-0810 to date, with no serious adverse events or pruritus reported; pharmacokinetic findings to date support sustained target engagement, including a half-life of eight weeks; and Data supporting advancement into patient study. ProQR plans to present the full dataset from the Phase 1 study of AX-0810, including Cohort 3, at a medical or scientific conference later this year. In July, the Company submitted a Clinical Trial Application (CTA) to the European Medicines Agency (EMA) to initiate a Phase 1 clinical trial of AX-0811, its next-generation editing oligonucleotide (EON) targeting NTCP for the treatment of cholestatic diseases. AX-0811 is generated by ProQR’s AI-enabled discovery engine and demonstrated higher potency and longer durability than AX-0810 preclinically, which will lead to lower dose levels and less frequent dosing in the clinic. Pending CTA authorization, initial data with AX-0811 is anticipated by year end 2026. ProQR continues preparations for an investigator-initiated trial (IIT) in pediatric biliary atresia in China, with initial clinical data expected in the first half of 2027. Strengthened Financial Position In June, ProQR closed an underwritten registered direct offering of $50.0 million, alongside a concurrent private placement to an existing shareholder and strategic partner Eli Lilly and Company (Lilly) of $9.2 million, for total gross proceeds of approximately $59.2 million. The financing further strengthened the Company’s balance sheet providing runway into mid-2028, and is expected to support the continued advancement of its wholly owned Axiomer RNA editing pipeline, including multiple anticipated clinical milestones. Platform and Research Progress ProQR continues to strengthen the scientific foundation of its Axiomer RNA editing platform through ongoing research and publication of preclinical findings. During the quarter, the Company’s preclinical research describing RNA editing of B4GALT1 was published online as a peer-reviewed Journal Pre-proof in Molecular Therapy – Nucleic Acids . The publication further expands the body of evidence supporting the breadth and versatility of the Axiomer platform beyond the Company’s clinical pipeline. Upcoming anticipated milestones NTCP franchise AX-0810 data from the 9 mg/kg cohort and 12-week follow up from the ongoing Phase 1 study expected by year-end 2026 AX-0811 initial data in healthy volunteers expected by year-end 2026, pending CTA authorization IIT in pediatric biliary atresia in China, with initial data targeted for first half of 2027 Potentially registration-enabling Phase 2 program, subject to regulatory interactions, expected to start in mid-2027 with first interim analysis data expected by mid-2028 Other pipeline candidates AX-0422 for MPS I Hurler Syndrome (IDUA) CTA filing for a first-in-patient study anticipated in early 2027 and initial data expected in the first half of 2027 AX-2911(PNPLA3) FIH IIT in China expected in the first half of 2027 Partnership Continue to execute on Lilly collaboration, with potential data updates and milestone payments Financial Highlights At June 30, 2026, ProQR held cash and cash equivalents of approximately € 117.1 million, compared to € 92.4 million at December 31, 2025. In June 2026, the Company closed an underwritten registered direct offering of 27,624,310 ordinary shares and a concurrent private placement of 5,100,780 ordinary shares with Lilly for gross proceeds totaling approximately $59.2 million. Net cash used in operating activities during the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 was € 12.3 million, compared to € 11.4 million used for the same period in 2025. Research and development (R&D) costs for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 were € 12.7 million, compared to € 11.4 million for the same period last year. General and administrative costs for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 were € 4.9 million, compared to € 4.8 million for the same period in 2025. Net loss for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was € 8.7 million, or € 0.08 per diluted share, compared to € 12.2 million, or € 0.12 per diluted share, for the same period in 2025. For further financial information for the period ended June 30, 2026, please refer to our Q2 financial report filing available on our website, www.proqr.com under Financials and Filings. About Axiomer ™ ProQR is pioneering a next-generation RNA base editing technology called Axiomer™, which could potentially yield a new class of medicines for diverse types of diseases. Axiomer™ “Editing Oligonucleotides”, or EONs, mediate single nucleotide changes to RNA in a highly specific and targeted way using molecular machinery that is present in human cells called ADAR (Adenosine Deaminase Acting on RNA). Axiomer™ EONs are designed to recruit and direct endogenously expressed ADARs to change an Adenosine (A) to an Inosine (I) in the RNA – an Inosine is translated as a Guanosine (G) – correcting an RNA with a disease-causing mutation back to a normal (wild type) RNA, modulating protein expression, or altering a protein so that it will have a new function that helps prevent or treat disease. About ProQR ProQR Therapeutics is a clinical-stage company dedicated to changing lives through the creation of transformative RNA therapies. ProQR is pioneering a next-generation RNA technology called Axiomer™, which uses a cell’s own editing machinery called ADAR to make specific single nucleotide edits in RNA to reverse a mutation or modulate protein expression and could potentially yield a new class of medicines for both rare and prevalent diseases with unmet need. Based on our unique proprietary RNA repair platform technologies we are growing our pipeline with patients and loved ones in mind. Learn more about ProQR at www.proqr.com . summary: Parents seeking affordability and safety in a used car for their teens shouldn’t need to compromise. CarGurus poured over NHTSA and IIHS data to list 10 budget-friendly safe vehicles, covering subcompact cars to minivans.
body_text: If you search online for "best cars for teen drivers," you'll quickly find yourself buried under an avalanche of guides. There's just one problem: most of them assume you're ready to spend $25,000 or more. That kind of budget opens up a wide range of new vehicles, but if you've been diligently saving for your kid's future—whether that means trade school, a four-year university, or something else entirely—$20,000 could cover a significant chunk of tuition and living expenses. That's why we're taking a different approach, focusing on used cars for young drivers that fit a genuinely realistic budget. Used car prices have pulled back substantially from their pandemic-era highs, which means finding something safe, reliable, and dependable for under $8,000 is far more achievable today than it was a few years ago. A few honest caveats before we dive in: vehicles like the BMW X3, Honda CR-V, Volvo XC60, and Mazda CX-5 are going to be nearly impossible to track down under this dollar amount. Likewise, any pickup truck in this price range will likely be older than most parents would prefer. That said, plenty of vehicles within this budget still deliver meaningful safety technology—airbags, stability control, and in some cases even automatic emergency braking and blind spot monitoring. Throughout this guide, we'll reference National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) crash test scores and—where available—Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) crash test data. It's worth keeping in mind that safety ratings are always evolving, as both organizations regularly update and tighten their testing standards. We're deliberately leaving coupes and sports cars off the list, concentrating instead on sedans, crossovers, EVs, and the reliably useful hatchback. Minivans, despite their reputation, are actually an outstanding choice for teen drivers—even if the teens themselves may need a little persuading. Here's a look at some of the strongest options available. What Makes CarGurus Best Cars Guides Different The Safest Used Cars Under $8,000 for Teens in 2026 2012 to 2024 Mitsubishi Mirage 2012 to 2017 Kia Rio 2011 to 2016 Nissan LEAF 2011 to 2016 Nissan Juke 2009 to 2014 Subaru Legacy 2007 to 2012 Toyota Highlander 2007 to 2008 Ford Edge 2010 to 2019 Ford Taurus 2009 to 2011 Ford Crown Victoria 2004 to 2010 Toyota Sienna FAQs Shopping Tools Related Topics Subcompact Car: 2012 to 2024 Mitsubishi Mirage NHTSA Crash Test Score: 4/5 Stars IIHS Overall Rating: Marginal IIHS Death Rate: 72/million miles traveled Let's get one thing out of the way upfront: subcompact and compact cars are inherently less protective than larger vehicles in a crash. That's just physics. Even so, certain small cars punch above their weight class, and the real-world fatality numbers back that up. At this price point, going smaller means you can target newer model years—which translates directly into more advanced safety technology that older vehicles simply don't have. The Mitsubishi Mirage isn't going to turn heads or win driving enthusiast awards—it's straightforward, fuel-efficient transportation that does its job better than waiting for a bus. It held up reasonably well across both NHTSA and IIHS evaluations, delivering a credible level of safety equipment for its segment without falling apart under scrutiny. Among vehicles its size, this little hatchback records one of the lowest death rates per million miles in the entire segment. As an added benefit, its light and responsive handling can actually help new drivers sharpen their car control instincts and hazard-avoidance skills. Read our Overview of the Mitsubishi Mirage Search for Mitsubishi Mirage See all 2023 Mitsubishi Mirage $7,499 54,222 miles No additional dealer fees No Rating Mckinney, TX 2024 Mitsubishi Mirage $7,999 69,943 miles Fees may apply No Rating Lexington, KY 2024 Mitsubishi Mirage $8,145 42,086 miles Includes dealer fees Uncertain Dallas, TX Subcompact Car: 2012 to 2017 Kia Rio NHTSA Crash Test Score: 4/5 Stars IIHS Overall Rating: Marginal IIHS Death Rate: 87/million miles traveled The Rio sits a rung above the Mirage in the used car pecking order. When Kia gave it a full redesign in 2012, the NHTSA responded with a four-star crash test score. The IIHS assigned it a "Marginal" rating—one step below its top "Good" score in 2014—primarily because the crash test dummy's head made only brief contact with the airbag before moving off to the left. That said, the IIHS confirmed that both the side and torso airbags deployed and provided meaningful protection. Its death rate is noticeably higher than the national average of 36, yet it still ranked as the second lowest among all small cars tracked in the IIHS database. Comparable alternatives exist from Kia's sister brand Hyundai, but overall, the Rio tends to deliver the best combination of value and safety for the money. These cars typically cost less than equivalent gas-powered alternatives, have demonstrated above-average reliability over the years, and earn solid marks on safety. We chose it over the hybrid Toyota Prius specifically to reduce ongoing maintenance costs and mechanical complexity. The IIHS did dock the LEAF for its frontal overlap crash test result, but it performed well across every other evaluation, and the NHTSA gave it a perfect five-star rating. Perhaps the most striking figure is the death rate: LEAF occupants have experienced roughly 10 percent of the fatalities per million miles traveled compared to Rio drivers. That's a compelling statistic no matter how you look at it. Its real-world death rate of 15 per million miles traveled comes in better than average, according to IIHS figures. One small caveat: pricing can occasionally nudge just past our $8,000 ceiling, though usually only by a small amount—and there's typically room to negotiate. On the running-cost front, the Juke delivers solid fuel economy, which helps keep day-to-day expenses manageable for a teen driver. The Toyota RAV4 is another legitimate contender in this category, but finding a clean example from a comparable model year under $8,000 is becoming increasingly difficult. The fifth-generation Subaru Legacy earned an IIHS Top Safety Pick—the organization's highest honor at the time—and received a five-star rating from the NHTSA. Even more remarkable: the IIHS database recorded zero fatalities for this generation of Legacy, which is an extraordinary result by any standard. For parents whose teen will be driving to a campus where winter weather is a real factor, the all-wheel drive Legacy sedan is a genuinely smart call. The trade-off is that staying under $8,000 will likely mean shopping for older examples, probably with close to 100,000 miles already on the clock. It's also worth noting that everything said here applies to the Outback wagon, though that model tends to carry a price premium—making the Legacy sedan the smarter choice for shoppers watching their budget. These second-generation Highlanders earned strong marks from the IIHS, taking home a "Top Safety Pick" award in 2009. The NHTSA tested them as well, though it didn't issue an overall rating for this era. In individual evaluations, the Highlander earned five stars for the front driver's side crash test and both side impact tests, with four stars for the front passenger and rollover categories. Its death rate runs notably higher than the Legacy's, which likely reflects the increased rollover risk that comes with a taller, heavier SUV body style. It also impressed the NHTSA, collecting five-star ratings for the driver's side front impact and both side crash tests, along with four stars for the front passenger and rollover evaluations. Most significantly, the IIHS database shows zero recorded deaths per million miles traveled for the Edge, placing it among the safest used vehicles you can find at any price point. The fact that it now reliably falls under the $8,000 threshold makes it one of the standout value picks on this entire list. It's a big, well-proportioned sedan with a roomy interior and more space than most teenagers will realistically need. The 2011 model earned a five-star NHTSA crash test rating and topped the IIHS charts with a "Good" score and a "Top Safety Pick" designation. Its overall death rate also comes in below the national average. You'll likely need to shop for examples with over 100,000 miles to stay under the $8,000 mark, but the Taurus has proven itself a genuinely durable vehicle over the long haul. And for what it's worth, it aged considerably more gracefully in terms of styling than rivals like the Chevrolet Malibu and Toyota Camry from the same period. The Crown Vic was never a standout student in the IIHS's increasingly demanding crash test curriculum. Built on a platform rooted in the early 1990s, it consistently earned five-star NHTSA ratings while managing only Marginal scores from the IIHS, particularly for side crash test performance and its dated head restraint and seat design. And yet, despite the millions of Crown Victorias that spent their working lives as taxi cabs and police cruisers, the 2011-era model recorded just 4 deaths per million miles traveled—a genuinely remarkable figure. Pricing varies wildly, from nearly free to well above $15,000 depending on condition and mileage. Minivans can match or outperform many crossover SUVs in real-world utility, and with the rear seats folded flat, there's enough cargo room to fit the whole band and every piece of their gear. Several strong options exist under $8,000, but the Subaru Legacy (2009–2014) and Ford Edge (2007–2008) stand out for their combination of IIHS Top Safety Pick awards and zero recorded fatalities per million miles traveled in IIHS data. The Nissan LEAF from 2011 to 2016 is also worth serious consideration, with a death rate of just 8 per million miles — roughly 10 percent of what some comparable small cars record. The right pick ultimately depends on your teen's driving environment, daily range needs, and whether features like all-wheel drive are a priority. Can you actually find a safe, reliable used car for under $8,000? Yes — used car prices have come down significantly from their pandemic-era highs, making it genuinely possible to find vehicles with meaningful safety features at this price point. Many cars in this budget still offer airbags, stability control, and in some cases automatic emergency braking and blind spot monitoring. The trade-off is that staying under $8,000 often means accepting higher mileage or reaching further back in the model year timeline, particularly for larger vehicles like midsize SUVs. Are small cars safe enough for teen drivers? Subcompact and compact cars are inherently less safe than larger vehicles due to basic physics, but some small cars perform meaningfully better than others in real-world crash data. The Mitsubishi Mirage, for example, records one of the lowest death rates per million miles in its segment, and choosing a smaller, less expensive car allows you to shop for newer model years with more up-to-date safety technology. If budget allows, stepping up to a midsize sedan or SUV will generally offer better crash protection. Is a minivan actually a good first car for a teen? It might sound like an unlikely choice, but a minivan like the 2004–2010 Toyota Sienna is genuinely one of the safer and more practical options on this list. The Sienna recorded zero deaths per million miles traveled in IIHS data, earned strong marks in NHTSA crash testing, and offers real-world utility that crossovers struggle to match. The bigger challenge may be convincing your teenager that it's cool — but the safety and practicality case is hard to argue with. What Makes CarGurus Best Cars Guides Different? Most car-shopping websites publish lists of the best cars across a variety of categories, with recommendations generally driven by editorial expertise. Here's what makes ours different: In addition to the insights and verdicts of our team of car-testing experts, our best cars guides take into account other factors that we know matter to buyers-real owner experiences and current market value. Our expert reviewers are among this country's most trusted automotive journalists, also writing for publications including US News and World Report, Edmunds, Digital Trends, J.D. Power, and Car & Driver. They put each car through real-world testing and create detailed reviews of performance in a range of categories, from practicality and driving manners to cost-effectiveness and safety. We also analyze hundreds of thousands of used car listings on CarGurus.com to track which models consistently offer the highest percentage of best deals relative to how many are listed for sale. Then we factor in reviews from owners-people who actually live with these cars every day. Our proprietary Best Cars algorithm then creates a final Overall CarGurus rating combining expert scores, user reviews, and the percentage of listings that have earned the Good or Great Deal rating. This multi-pronged approach reveals not just which cars excel on paper, but which ones deliver satisfaction and value when you're ready to buy. body_text: Disney+ and Hulu Expand Library to Also Include Collection of iHeartPodcasts Desperately Devoted, Fake Doctors, Real Friends with Zach and Donald, Pod Meets World, StraightioLab and Thanks Dad with Ego Nwodim Download assets HERE Burbank, Calif. (August 10, 2026) – Disney+ and Hulu today announced a video podcasting deal with iHeartMedia for six iHeartPodcasts titles, beginning with Hey Jonas! on Disney+ and Hulu streaming August 14. Adding to its growing slate of licensed, rewatch, and companion podcasts, the collaboration will also bring video editions of iHeartPodcasts’ Pod Meets World to Disney+ as well as Desperately Devoted, Fake Doctors, Real Friends with Zach and Donald, StraightioLab, and Thanks Dad with Ego Nwodim to Hulu and Hulu on Disney+ for bundle subscribers in the U.S. in the coming months. New episodes will stream weekly across all podcasts. “Fans can’t get enough of the stories and talent they love, and podcasts have become one of the fastest growing ways for audiences to connect with them,” said Lauren Tempest, Head of Content Planning & Partnerships, DTC at The Walt Disney Company. “These new video podcasts from iHeartMedia bring fans closer to their favorite worlds and the creators behind them, and we’re thrilled to make them available on Disney+ and Hulu as part of an even richer streaming experience.” “Podcasting continues to evolve as audiences increasingly want to engage with the shows and personalities they love in more ways and across more platforms,” said Bob Pittman, Chairman and CEO for iHeartMedia. “Disney+ and Hulu have built powerful streaming destinations with incredibly passionate fan communities, making them ideal partners to expand the reach of these beloved iHeartPodcasts. From iconic rewatch series and fan-favorite conversations to original storytelling, this deal gives both existing listeners and new viewers an easy way to discover and connect with some of podcasting’s most engaging voices through video.” Leading up to the premiere of Camp Rock 3 on Disney+, Hey Jonas! will simultaneously debut on Disney+ and Hulu on August 14 with a new episode highlighting Camp Rock , and will continue with additional episodes of Kevin, Joe, and Nick Jonas live at D23: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event that weekend. Desperately Devoted on Hulu will begin streaming with video for the first time on November 2, making for the perfect time to catch up on Desperate Housewives episodes before diving even deeper with award-winning actress Teri Hatcher, her on-screen daughter Andrea Bowen, and her real-life daughter Emerson Tenney. Fans of Scrubs can also revisit each episode of the hit series alongside co-stars and real-life best friends Zach Braff and Donald Faison with Fake Doctors, Real Friends with Zach and Donald, streaming on Hulu beginning later this year. This expansion joins the existing lineup of podcasts on Disney+ and Hulu including licensed titles like Handsome and We’re Here to Help , in addition to rewatch podcasts like The Mess Around with Hannah and Lamorne , Prison Breaking With Sarah and Paul , and That Was Us . Companion podcasts are also available for Disney+ and Hulu's most popular series, such as Paradise , American Idol , and Dancing with the Stars , as well as FX’s The Shards and Love Story: John F. Kennedy Jr. & Carolyn Bessette . The full list of podcasts currently streaming can be found in the ”Podcasts” Collection on Disney+ and the “Podcasts” Hub on Hulu. Hey Jonas! Streams August 14 on Disney+ and Hulu The official Jonas Brothers podcast. Hosted by Kevin, Joe, and Nick Jonas. It’s the Jonas Brothers you know... musicians, actors, and well, yes, brothers. Now, they’re sharing another side of themselves in the playful, intimate, and irreverent way only they can. Spend time with the Jonas Brothers here and stay a little bit longer for deep conversations like never before. Pod Meets World Streams August 24 on Disney+ After recapping all 7 seasons of Boy Meets World the sitcom they starred in as teenagers, and now with over 55 million audio downloads to their name, Danielle Fishel, Will Friedle and Rider Strong are taking their 30-year friendship to the next level. This newest chapter of the podcast will dig deeper into their undeniable chemistry through more shared ‘90s memories, random tangents, new side quests and exciting guests. They’re back for a new era – so fans can join their three childhood best friends on Pod Meets World! Desperately Devoted Streams November 2 on Hulu Dear Neighbor, Welcome back to Wisteria Lane. Viewers are cordially invited to Desperately Devoted—a re-watch of the groundbreaking show Desperate Housewives . Viewers are welcome to wander with the hosts as they stroll past the picket fences, and straight into the homes and hearts of Wisteria Lane. Hosted by award-winning actress Teri Hatcher, her on-screen daughter Andrea Bowen, and her real-life daughter Emerson Tenney, this podcast brings together three women with distinct perspectives to reflect on the iconic storylines and characters that resonated across generations, turning the show into a global phenomenon. While rewatching the series, the hosts use its themes as a springboard for broader conversations on women’s issues, relationships, parenting, sex, identity, and more, with warmth and humor. Teri and Andrea share insider insight and firsthand memories, while Emerson brings a fresh, modern perspective as she watches the full series for the first time. Each week, these BFFs will discuss an episode of Scrubs, sharing behind-the-scenes stories and reminiscing on some of their favorite memories from filming. They’ll also connect with Scrubs super fans and feature beloved show cast members for exclusive interviews. StraightioLab Streams in the Fall on Hulu StraightioLab is an intellectual podcast where smart comedians George Civeris and Sam Taggart unpack the rich, multi-colored tapestry of straight culture. Each episode investigates a different "straight topic," from college fraternities and gender reveal parties to overhead lighting and themed restaurants. Over the last six years, George and Sam have welcomed countless superstar guests to the studio, toured the country, and been showered with accolades from once-prestigious magazines that have since made the switch to vertical video. Next stop? Winning the streaming wars once and for all. Thanks Dad with Ego Nwodim Streams in the Fall on Hulu Raised by a single mom, Ego Nwodim may have daddy issues, but she suspects she’s in good company. Ego has funny, heartfelt conversations with her guests about the good, the bad and the not-so-pretty that have shaped their trajectories and made them who they are. title: Firebird Launches CIS Region’s Largest AI Factory in Armenia
summary: The global buildout of AI infrastructure reached a new milestone today — Firebird, an emerging AI cloud, launched the CIS region’s largest AI factory in Armenia, establishing a new AI computing hub powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing and Dell Technologies high-performance AI infrastructure.
